newsitem.title: THAILAND: First Thai planes arrive in Bangkok from Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: First Thai planes arrive in Bangkok from Cambodia.

text.p: The first Thai Airforce C-130 plane arrived in Bangkok from Cambodia on Tuesday, carrying dozens of Thais and other foreigners who fled fighting in Phnom Penh.

Thailand's foreign minister and other senior officials were on the tarmac to meet the plane, filled mostly with women and children. It was the first of three planes that took off from Phnom Penh's battered airport earlier on Tuesday.
The first plane arrived around 0500 GMT and two others were due to follow soon afterwards.
The foreigners who were on the planes were among several hundred people waiting at Phnom Penh's airport on Tuesday to escape the Cambodian capital after three days of fighting and turmoil.

Thai air force commandos accompanying the aircraft formed a perimeter around the planes as people ran towards them to try to flee the city. A Thai official organising the evacuation in Phnom Penh said the planes should each make at least one more trip on Tuesday, making for a total of six flights. Officials hoped to take up to 700 people out of the country.

Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said in Bangkok on Tuesday that apart from more than 700 Thai citizens, some 120 Americans, 100 New Zealanders and 300 Pakistanis had also requested to join the flights. Other countries had requested help and the Thai ambassador in Phnom Penh said Thailand could help evacuate foreign nationals on Wednesday.
